points.place: 法国诺曼底地区布兰维尔
points.title: 早年艺术启蒙
points.description: 马塞尔·杜尚出生于法国诺曼底的一个艺术世家，父亲是一名公证人，母亲是一位业余艺术家。杜尚是七个孩子中最小的，其中两个哥哥雅克-维龙和雷蒙·杜尚-维龙后来也成为艺术家。这个家庭环境为杜尚提供了早期的艺术熏陶，但他的教育主要是在公立学校完成的。这段时期，杜尚对数学和哲学产生了浓厚兴趣，这些学科后来深刻影响了他对艺术的思考方式。
points.descriptionEn: Marcel Duchamp was born in Blainville, Normandy, France, into an artistic family. His father was a notary, and his mother was an amateur artist. Duchamp was the youngest of seven children, two of whom, Jacques Villon and Raymond Duchamp-Villon, also became artists. This family environment provided Duchamp with early artistic exposure, though his education was primarily in public schools. During this period, Duchamp developed a strong interest in mathematics and philosophy, which would later profoundly influence his approach to art.

points.title: 前卫艺术探索
points.description: 1904年，杜尚搬到巴黎，开始全职从事艺术创作。他最初受到印象派和后印象派的影响，但很快转向了更具实验性的风格。1909年，他创作了《下楼的裸女二号》，这件作品后来成为立体主义的代表作之一。在巴黎期间，杜尚与当时的前卫艺术圈密切交往，包括毕加索、布拉克等艺术家。1912年，他的作品《下楼的裸女二号》被立体主义画展拒绝，这促使他开始质疑传统艺术的价值和意义。
points.descriptionEn: In 1904, Duchamp moved to Paris and began working full-time as an artist. Initially influenced by Impressionism and Post-Impressionism, he quickly shifted to more experimental styles. In 1909, he created 'Nude Descending a Staircase, No. 2,' which later became one of the key works of Cubism. During his time in Paris, Duchamp was closely associated with the avant-garde art circle, including artists like Picasso and Braque. In 1912, his 'Nude Descending a Staircase, No. 2' was rejected by the Cubist exhibition, prompting him to question the value and meaning of traditional art.

points.title: 达达主义先驱
points.description: 1912年至1915年间，杜尚开始创作一系列挑战传统艺术观念的作品。1913年，他创作了《自行车轮》，这是一件现成品艺术，将自行车轮倒置在凳子上，挑战了艺术必须由艺术家亲手创造的传统观念。1915年，他创作了最具争议的作品《喷泉》，这是一件签名的陶瓷小便池，提交给独立艺术家展览。这件作品被拒绝，但后来成为20世纪最具影响力的艺术作品之一。这一时期，杜尚开始思考艺术与生活的关系，提出了'艺术不是视觉的，而是思想的'这一革命性观点。
points.descriptionEn: Between 1912 and 1915, Duchamp began creating works that challenged traditional artistic concepts. In 1913, he created 'Bicycle Wheel,' a readymade artwork consisting of a bicycle wheel mounted upside down on a stool, challenging the notion that art must be created by the artist's hand. In 1915, he created his most controversial work, 'Fountain,' a signed urinal submitted to the Society of Independent Artists. Though rejected, it later became one of the most influential artworks of the 20th century. During this period, Duchamp began contemplating the relationship between art and life, proposing the revolutionary idea that 'art is not visual, it's thought.'

points.title: 美国艺术影响
points.description: 1915年，杜尚为躲避第一次世界大战移居纽约。在纽约期间，他与曼·雷、弗朗西斯·毕卡比亚等艺术家密切合作，共同推动了美国前卫艺术的发展。1917年，他协助组织了独立艺术家展览，并提交了《喷泉》。1920年，他与毕卡比亚和曼·雷共同创办了《盲人》杂志，探索艺术与文学的新形式。这一时期，杜尚继续创作现成品艺术，并开始创作大型作品《大玻璃》(The Large Glass)，这是一件未完成的装置艺术作品，体现了他对机械和艺术的独特思考。
points.descriptionEn: In 1915, Duchamp moved to New York to escape World War I. During his time in New York, he worked closely with artists like Man Ray and Francis Picabia, jointly promoting the development of American avant-garde art. In 1917, he assisted in organizing the Independent Artists exhibition and submitted 'Fountain.' In 1920, he co-founded the magazine 'The Blind Man' with Picabia and Man Ray, exploring new forms of art and literature. During this period, Duchamp continued creating readymades and began working on his large-scale work 'The Large Glass,' an unfinished installation that reflected his unique thinking about machinery and art.

points.title: 国际艺术交流
points.description: 1923年至1941年间，杜尚在巴黎和纽约之间频繁往返，成为连接欧洲和美国艺术界的重要桥梁。1923年，他完成了《大玻璃》，并开始创作一系列基于光学错觉的作品，如《旋转的玻璃盘》。1926年，他参与设计了巴黎的超现实主义展览。1930年代，杜尚开始对国际象棋产生浓厚兴趣，甚至曾代表法国参加国际象棋奥林匹克比赛。他将国际象棋视为一种艺术形式，认为其策略性和创造性与艺术创作有相似之处。这一时期，杜尚逐渐淡出艺术创作，转而专注于策展和艺术理论工作。
points.descriptionEn: Between 1923 and 1941, Duchamp frequently traveled between Paris and New York, becoming an important bridge connecting European and American art circles. In 1923, he completed 'The Large Glass' and began creating a series of works based on optical illusions, such as 'Rotating Glass Plates.' In 1926, he participated in designing the Surrealist exhibition in Paris. During the 1930s, Duchamp developed a keen interest in chess, even representing France in the Chess Olympiad. He viewed chess as an art form, believing its strategic and creative aspects were similar to artistic creation. During this period, Duchamp gradually stepped away from creating art, focusing instead on curating and art theory.

points.title: 晚年艺术遗产
points.description: 1941年，杜尚定居纽约，直到1968年去世。这一时期，他继续参与艺术界的活动，但创作减少，转而专注于艺术理论和策展工作。1950年代，杜尚的作品开始获得广泛认可，对后来的波普艺术、概念艺术产生了深远影响。1963年，他在纽约现代艺术博物馆举办了首次大型回顾展。杜尚晚年致力于整理自己的作品和理论，为后世留下了丰富的艺术遗产。他的'现成品'概念彻底改变了人们对艺术的理解，为后来的观念艺术奠定了基础。1968年，杜尚在法国逝世，享年81岁。
points.descriptionEn: In 1941, Duchamp settled in New York, where he remained until his death in 1968. During this period, he continued to be active in the art world but created less, focusing instead on art theory and curating. In the 1950s, Duchamp's work gained widespread recognition, profoundly influencing later Pop Art and Conceptual Art. In 1963, he had his first major retrospective at the Museum of Modern Art in New York. In his later years, Duchamp dedicated himself to organizing his works and theories, leaving a rich artistic legacy for future generations. His concept of the 'readymade' completely changed people's understanding of art, laying the foundation for later Conceptual Art. Duchamp died in France in 1968 at the age of 81.

appraisal.zh: 杜尚被视为20世纪艺术的关键转折人物，他以「现成品」打破艺术须由艺术家亲手创造的传统，把艺术从视觉体验提升到思想层面，为概念艺术、波普艺术和装置艺术开辟道路，其影响还扩展到哲学与文化研究。另一种看法认为，他的现成品缺乏技巧与创造力，其「反艺术」立场反而造就新的精英主义，加深了艺术与大众的疏离。无论如何，他留下的问题至今仍在艺术界引发思考。
appraisal.en: Duchamp is seen as the pivotal turning point of twentieth-century art: his readymades broke the notion that art must be made by the artist's hand, raised art from visual experience to the conceptual level, opened the way for Conceptual, Pop and Installation art, and extended his influence into philosophy and cultural studies. Another view holds that his readymades lack skill and creativity, and that his anti-art stance bred a new elitism and deepened the estrangement between art and the public. Either way, the questions he posed still provoke debate.

supporter.zh: 杜尚被视为20世纪最具革命性的艺术家之一，他彻底改变了人们对艺术的定义。通过引入'现成品'概念，杜尚打破了艺术必须由艺术家亲手创造的传统观念，将艺术从视觉体验提升到思想层面。他的作品《喷泉》和《大玻璃》等挑战了艺术与日常物品的界限，为后来的概念艺术、波普艺术和装置艺术开辟了道路。杜尚的艺术理念强调艺术家的自由选择和观众的参与，这种民主化的艺术观念对当代艺术产生了深远影响。
supporter.en: Duchamp is regarded as one of the most revolutionary artists of the 20th century, who completely transformed the definition of art. By introducing the concept of the 'readymade,' Duchamp broke the traditional notion that art must be created by the artist's hand, elevating art from a visual experience to a conceptual level. His works like 'Fountain' and 'The Large Glass' challenged the boundaries between art and everyday objects, paving the way for later Conceptual Art, Pop Art, and Installation Art. Duchamp's artistic philosophy emphasized the artist's freedom of choice and audience participation, a democratic approach that has profoundly influenced contemporary art.

critic.zh: 批评者认为杜尚的艺术观念过于精英化和反传统，有时甚至被视为对艺术本身的否定。他的现成品作品被批评为缺乏技巧和创造力，仅仅是对现成物品的简单挪用。一些评论家指出，杜尚的'反艺术'立场实际上创造了一种新的艺术精英主义，只有少数人能够理解其作品的深层含义。此外，他的作品《喷泉》等也被批评为对艺术传统的嘲弄，缺乏对艺术史的尊重。批评者认为，杜尚的艺术革命虽然具有启发性，但也导致了艺术与大众之间的进一步疏离。
critic.en: Critics argue that Duchamp's artistic concepts are overly elitist and anti-traditional, sometimes even seen as negating art itself. His readymade works have been criticized for lacking skill and creativity, merely being simple appropriations of existing objects. Some commentators suggest that Duchamp's 'anti-art' stance actually created a new artistic elitism, understandable only by a select few who could grasp the deeper meanings of his works. Additionally, pieces like 'Fountain' have been criticized as mocking artistic tradition, lacking respect for art history. Critics believe that while Duchamp's artistic revolution was inspiring, it also led to further alienation between art and the general public.

objective.zh: 在历史学界和流行文化中，杜尚被定义为现代艺术的关键转折点人物。他的作品和理念不仅影响了艺术本身，还扩展到了哲学、社会学和文化研究领域。杜尚的'现成品'概念成为20世纪艺术理论的核心议题，引发了关于艺术本质、原创性和艺术价值的持续讨论。在流行文化中，杜尚的形象常常被简化为'反叛艺术家'的象征，但学术界更倾向于将他视为一位复杂的思想家，其艺术实践体现了对艺术体制的深刻批判。杜尚的遗产不仅体现在他的作品上，更体现在他提出的问题和挑战中，这些问题至今仍在艺术界引发思考。
objective.en: In academic and popular culture, Duchamp is defined as a pivotal figure in the transition to modern art. His works and ideas have influenced not only art itself but also extended into philosophy, sociology, and cultural studies. Duchamp's concept of the 'readymade' has become a central topic in 20th-century art theory, sparking ongoing discussions about the nature of art, originality, and artistic value. In popular culture, Duchamp is often simplified as a symbol of the 'rebellious artist,' but academia tends to view him as a complex thinker whose artistic practice embodied a profound critique of the art establishment. Duchamp's legacy lies not only in his works but in the questions and challenges he posed, which continue to provoke thought in the art world today.

self.zh: 艺术不是视觉的，而是思想的。
self.en: Art is not visual, it's thought.
